items.title: Adolphe Alexander Interview, 1961-03-08
items.q: The name 'Ralph Collins' is mentioned only in the interviewer's closing statement listing other musicians ('Harold Dajon and Ralph Collins and this is Bill Russell'), with no interaction or personal connection described by the interviewee.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Until the auditorium. Well, I think we've covered your life pretty well, unless you can think of some other

question. Anything else, Ralph? Think of anywhere else you played? Any musicians? Well, anywhere else I played? Yeah. In places like that. I don't too well. Like on the lake. You played a whole lot of campsite on the lake, I know. Oh, well I played a whole lot of little

single job with different guys. Yeah, yeah. Well, who? Where? Oh, oh. Hundreds of them, I guess. I played with a whole lot of people. I was telling you, I was telling you of the bands that I played with. But besides that, oh, I played a whole lot of little combinations. Five and six combinations. You know that. I played with you a lot of times. I know that. I played with you. With a combination. Did you ever play with a violin in the band? Yeah. I used to play with the cellar. But the cellar that died.
